reuse.why: Routes every month-wide action, including the new last-month-spending one, through the existing getBulkBudgetCategories selector, and reuses extractTagsFromText, getSheetValue, averageToBudget, setBudget and the mutator/undoable registration.

duplication.why: Each exclusion rule (hidden, #fixed group tag, saved template) is written once in the shared selector; the new action does not copy any existing action body.

placement.why: Category selection stays in the bulk-action selector in budget/actions.ts and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts beside its siblings.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests, but includes an unrelated import reorder in server/schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: A single documented selector with one optional flag is easy to own; reusing averageToBudget for a one-month spending amount is a slight naming stretch.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth, setZero, setLastMonthSpending and the 3/6/12-month averages all take their categories from getBulkBudgetCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the template check is a small new helper rather than a reshaped copy.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories keeps two parameters (includeHidden renamed to includeHiddenCategories rather than a new flag added); the #fixed and template checks are general rules applying to every caller, and the new action calls the selector.
